audit.whatIsWrong: diff is EVEN while tone is #ff5d6c (the hard-lane red), diffRating is 8.5/10, and report[14] reads 'Hard matchup'. Three fields say hard, one says even.
audit.why: 49.8% over 504 games with an 8.5 difficulty is a hard lane, and every other field on the page already agrees. EVEN is the outlier.
audit.corrected: diff EVEN -> HARD. tone, diffRating and report[14] need no change — they were already right.

audit.why: Teemo owns levels 1-2 and the late map; Cho'Gath's windows are level 6 and the first health item. The prose has this right — it is a lane you survive and a map you lose, not a lane you win.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three stages contradict the page's own whys[]. whys[2] says Carnivore and Rupture's slow 'let you farm through his poke and contest trades to stabilize the lane' but Level 3 is scored Teemo; whys[4] says Feast 'turns any step into Rupture range into a kill threat' but Level 6 is scored Teemo; whys[5] says 'you shove him under tower' but First item is scored Skill.
audit.why: The packet chart matches those three whys. Level 6 in particular cannot be Teemo's — Noxious Trap is a zoning tool that adds nothing to a duel, while Feast is a true-damage execute against the lowest health pool in the matchup.
audit.corrected: Level 3 Skill (5/10), Level 6 Cho'Gath (6/10), First item Cho'Gath (6/10). Proposed as one atomic chart group across both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet defect is real: the content layer never names a single Teemo ability, using 'his Q blind', 'his E poison', 'his R shrooms' throughout. Beyond the naming, three mechanics are missing or wrong. (a) Guerrilla Warfare is absent entirely — Teemo goes invisible standing still, keeps invisibility while MOVING in brush, and leaves stealth with bonus attack speed. An immobile Cho'Gath facechecking lane brush is the worst thing he can do, and the page never says it. (b) Move Quick's passive speed is lost the moment an enemy champion or turret strikes him, so a single Vorpal Spikes proc strips the kite — the page instead presents his speed as unanswerable. (c) Noxious Trap bounces off another mushroom for extra range, which is how he threatens ground he never walks on. (d) The donts entry 'Stack pure HP vs his %damage' implies percent-health damage Teemo does not have — Toxic Shot is flat on-hit magic damage plus a 4-second DoT.
audit.why: Riot text — Guerrilla Warfare: 'If Teemo stands still and takes no actions for a short duration, he becomes Invisible indefinitely. If he's in brush, Teemo can enter and maintain his Invisibility while moving. After leaving Invisibility, Teemo gains the Element of Surprise, increasing his Attack Speed.' Blinding Dart: 7s flat, 680 range, projectile. Move Quick: 14s, 'passively increasing his Move Speed until he is struck by an enemy champion or turret'. Toxic Shot: no cooldown, on-hit, damage on impact and each second for 4 seconds. Noxious Trap: 0.25s, 600/750/900 range, 'If Teemo throws a mushroom onto another mushroom it will bounce, gaining additional range.'
audit.corrected: Every content field I touched now uses Blinding Dart, Toxic Shot, Move Quick and Noxious Trap by name. Guerrilla Warfare's brush stealth and Element of Surprise added to dontsFull[2]; Move Quick's strip-on-hit added to wants.foe[1] and breakdown.cooldowns; the mushroom bounce added to dontsFull[1].d and wants.foe[2]; the invented percent-damage framing removed from dontsFull[2].t.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns named Blinding Dart with no number, and the whole page frames the blind as though it shuts Cho'Gath down entirely.
audit.why: Blinding Dart is 7 seconds flat at every rank and it blinds BASIC ATTACKS. Rupture and Feral Scream land through it untouched — which is the single most useful thing a Cho'Gath player can know here, and the page only gestured at it with 'Q-poke instead'.
audit.corrected: The autos-only rule and the 7s figure stated plainly in dosFull[0].d, report[5].t, breakdown.cooldowns and phases[2].why.

notes:
PACKET DISAGREEMENT LEFT UNRESOLVED, deliberately. The packet levelChart gives 2+ items to Skill, but this page's whys[6] ('he reclaims the lane on the open map'), spikes[3].text and the late paragraph all say Teemo, and Teemo genuinely does own the late map against a champion with no gap-closer. I left that row as Teemo — no edit — rather than invent a power shift the prose does not support. Flagging it so the packet snapshot can be checked.

DERIVED-FLAG MISFIRE: Teemo's Noxious Trap carries a 'knockup: displacement' flag. Riot's description says the trap 'will release a poisonous cloud, slowing enemies and damaging them over time' — no displacement of any kind. I did not write knockup anywhere for it.

UNVERIFIED, left as written: the page states that Blinding Dart's blind also eats the Vorpal Spikes proc riding on a blinded auto. Riot ties Vorpal Spikes to Cho'Gath's attacks, so it is a reasonable reading, but the kit files cannot confirm whether a blinded attack still releases the spikes. I kept the existing claim and did not build any new advice on it.

The packet's suspectName "Feral Scream's" in wants.you[1] is a FALSE POSITIVE — correct name, possessive form.
